title: Getting Great Results from AI
summary: Practical prompting skills: clear asks, good context, and checking the output.

lessons.title: Be clear and specific
points: Say what you want, who it's for and what 'good' looks like: "Write a 100-word update for non-technical staff about Friday's system maintenance."
Vague prompts get generic answers. Specific prompts get useful ones.
Ask for a format: bullet points, a table, a short email, a step-by-step list.

lessons.title: Give context and examples
points: Share relevant background (only what you're allowed to share) so the AI doesn't have to guess.
Show an example of the style or structure you want. Examples are very effective.
Break big tasks into steps, and review each step before moving on.

lessons.title: Iterate
points: Treat the first answer as a draft. Ask for changes: shorter, simpler, more formal, add an example.
Ask the AI to list its assumptions or what it's unsure about.
If it goes off track, start a fresh conversation with a better prompt.

lessons.title: Check before you use
points: Verify facts, figures, quotes and links against trusted sources.
Check tone and accuracy, especially for anything sent to customers or published.
Never include confidential data unless the tool is approved for it.
lessons.tip: Good prompt + human review = great result.

questions.q: Which prompt is likely to get the most useful result?
options: Write a friendly 120-word email to new staff explaining how to report phishing, with 3 bullet points
questions.why: It states the audience, purpose, length, tone and format.

questions.q: Giving the AI an example of the style you want usually improves the output.
questions.why: Examples show the model exactly what you mean, which is often clearer than a description.

questions.q: The AI's first draft is too long and too technical. What should you do?
options: Ask it to shorten and simplify for your audience
Copy it into a different AI unchanged
questions.why: Iterating with clear feedback is the fastest way to a good result.

questions.q: Once you have a good prompt, you can skip checking the facts in the answer.
questions.why: Even great prompts can produce errors. Always verify important facts and sources.

questions.q: What's a good way to handle a complex task with AI?
options: One giant prompt with everything at once
Break it into smaller steps and review each one
questions.why: Smaller steps make it easier to guide the AI and catch mistakes early.

questions.q: You want the AI's answer as a comparison you can paste into a slide. What should you add to the prompt?
options: Ask for a table with specific columns
questions.why: Specifying the output format, such as a table with named columns, gives you something ready to use.

questions.q: Asking the AI to state its assumptions can help you spot mistakes.
questions.why: Surfacing assumptions shows you where the answer might not fit your situation.

questions.q: Which context is appropriate to share with a public AI tool?
options: General description of your goal and audience
questions.why: Share the goal and audience, not sensitive data, unless the tool is approved for that data.
